body:
## Status and decision

**In Progress — redesign authorized; not fixed or production qualified.** No patch date is promised.

The owner has explicitly authorized redesign of the legacy PBF pressure/volume reconstruction using a geometry-consistent pressure backend. Develop and verify subcell geometry, conservative particle transfer and runtime timing before treating the reference method as an integrated production solution.

## Confirmed problem

The old Advanced Fluid Dynamics coupling inferred whole-body buoyancy/force across dry gaps. A spacecraft approximately 1.78–1.8 m clear of the particles received a huge force after water hit terrain and launched. Water beside a vertical face also generated impossible upward support.

The retained M100 report explains the false wet-volume path: body-wide reconstruction support and extrapolated column occupancy/material acceleration fed an invalid buoyancy load into the rigid body. Its original reproduction records 1.7759 m clearance, 0.1671 inferred wet fraction and an 85,212 N force. This is evidence of bad fluid coupling, not proof of a general rigid-body solver defect.

## Findings and failed approaches

The following later investigation results are confirmed findings supplied by the owner for this tracking issue; they are not presented as a fresh rerun or as production qualification:

| Approach | Result and limitation |
|---|---|
| Radius/extrapolation restrictions | Broke 15 immersion/support checks. Other prototypes prevented launch but failed buoyancy/flotation. The earlier M100 footprint-only experiment is a separate rejected trial with 8/93 failures; do not conflate these counts. |
| Coupled projection | Passed 1,100 conservation/admissibility checks. One frozen solve converged in 129 iterations at residual 6.25e-6, taking approximately 16.5 ms. Integrated buoyancy still failed. A frozen solve is not a runtime performance qualification. |
| Manufactured-pressure stencil | Fluid-only stencil produced 78.5% of expected buoyancy. Boundary unknowns produced 102.9%, but were poorly conditioned. |
| Affine reconstruction and contact-only approaches | Failed integrated buoyancy. |
| Geometry-consistent pressure-grid reference | Passes hydrostatic loading, floating/sinking and rotated gravity. This is mathematical/reference-prototype evidence, not an integrated, production-qualified backend. |

Retain the failed approaches and their original evidence. Preventing the spacecraft launch alone is insufficient if legitimate fluid support is lost.

## Scope and safeguards

- Advanced Fluids only. Preserve Basic Water and swimming, M54 conserved quantities, M55 surface flow and existing saves where applicable.
- Keep published Alpha v1.0.0 and `main` untouched. Development and validation belong in Experimental/isolated research work.
- Keep the Alpha advanced-fluid lockout intact until independently validated. This issue does not authorize publication, promotion or removal of the lockout.
- Preserve authored fluid data and original saves; document compatibility and migration requirements rather than silently converting or discarding data.

## Implementation and evidence work

- [ ] Develop geometry-consistent pressure/volume reconstruction with subcell solid/free-surface geometry and physically valid support boundaries.
- [ ] Develop conservative particle-to-grid/grid-to-particle transfer and consistent solid coupling.
- [ ] Integrate the backend into the actual Advanced Fluids runtime and measure convergence, conditioning and full runtime cost against explicit budgets.
- [ ] Record exact source/build identity, fixtures, commands, thresholds, raw results and timing conditions. Keep mathematical tests, frozen solves and integrated runtime evidence separately identified.
- [ ] Preserve a failed-approach register and link subsequent implementation reports and validation artifacts here.

## Acceptance gates — all still open

Use the original regression thresholds and negative controls; do not relax them to obtain a pass.

- [ ] No dry-gap or side-only false buoyancy; no spacecraft launch in the original and raised-water reproductions, with advanced-off controls.
- [ ] Correct half/full immersion, hydrostatic loading, flotation and sinking.
- [ ] Rotation covariance/rotated gravity; falling-water impacts; light bodies; common freefall; disconnected pools without false support transfer.
- [ ] Conservation of mass and momentum, passive-energy behavior and contact admissibility through integrated interaction.
- [ ] Convergence within declared solver budgets, with conditioning and failure behavior documented.
- [ ] Runtime performance measured in representative integrated scenes, including disturbed/contact cases; frozen-solve timing alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Cold saves/load, streaming and lifecycle checks, including applicable legacy-save compatibility and preservation of authored data.
- [ ] Basic Water/swimming, M54 conserved quantities and M55 surface-flow regressions remain within their original thresholds.
- [ ] Independent validation of the exact integrated candidate before any proposal to lift the Alpha lockout or publish a patch.

## Existing reports and context

- [M100 fluid contact-stability restriction and rejected local repair](https://github.com/SuperReaper1999/Project-Judas/blob/Experimental/docs/M100_FLUID_CONTACT_STABILITY.md)
- [Retained reproduction evidence and instructions](https://github.com/SuperReaper1999/Project-Judas/tree/Experimental/docs/evidence/m100/fluid-contact-stability)
- [Basic Water preview and preserved behavior](https://github.com/SuperReaper1999/Project-Judas/blob/Experimental/docs/M100_BASIC_WATER_PREVIEW.md)

Open and closed repository issues were checked before creation; no matching pressure-backend redesign issue was found. Later research numbers above are owner-provided findings; the linked M100 report documents the earlier bounded investigation and should not be cited as proof of every later result.
title: Advanced Fluid Dynamics: redesign the pressure backend with geometry-consistent coupling
